lines: They opened it. Just like that, after five weeks of it being a week.
Which tells me they finished. Not that they were ever going to say so.
Go and look at the stakes before somebody thinks to pull them up.
Under the road, is it. Under the road.
My grandmother said the same about the well down in Marrow Hollow.
Nobody believed her either. She was right, and it did her no good at all.
Ashgate used to be the last stop before the north road.
Now it's just the last stop.
Ask the gate fellow how his survey's coming. Watch his face, not his answer.
It's OPEN. I'm allowed now, so it's boring now.
That isn't fair and I would like somebody official to say so.
I'm not allowed past the gate.
I've been past the gate four times.
There's nothing there. Stakes, string, and a man writing numbers in a little book.

ag_house_a: Waystation's free, you know. Always has been.
The Concord offered to pay for a new roof on it last spring. We said no.
Then it rained through October and we said yes. It's a very good roof.
That's how it goes. Nobody buys you. They just fix things until you owe them.

lines: Word came back down the road about you. Roxen doesn't part with Seals.
I'll write to Vess tonight and tell him. He'll be unbearable about it.
He'll have earned it. Let him.
You're the one Vess sent out, then. He wrote ahead. Three pages.
Two and a half of them were about currents. The rest was about you.
Take care on Route 1 after dark. Things come down off the ridge.

ag_traveller: Walked in from the coast. Six days, and I'd happily do five of them again.
It's the sea. Flat wrong, not storm wrong. There's a difference.
Get out far enough and it doesn't move at all. Not a swell. Nothing.

lines: Corridor's done. Every forty metres to the coast, every one of them logged.
You'd think finishing would feel like something.
I've kept the last page in my coat. Read it nine times. Still nothing.
Depth soundings. Every forty metres, all the way down to the coast.
No, I don't know what we're listening for. Nobody tells the one holding the rod.
I know it answers, though. Not always. But sometimes it answers.
You can wade now. I can tell by how you're standing at the edge.
Far bank, behind the reeds. It's sat there since spring and I can't reach it.
Bring it back or don't. I'd just like to know what it is.
Pond's fine. Pond's normal. Pond does what a pond does.
It's the SEA that's gone strange, and nobody takes that from a pond man.
Come back when you can wade. There's something on the far bank.
Twenty crates up that road and now they want them all brought back down.
Same stakes. Same weight. Same me.
Don't tell me it's finished. Finished has a shape and that isn't it.
Four crates of survey stakes a week, up the north road.
Four a week for five weeks, and the road is still shut.
You do the arithmetic. I just carry them.
